hook_text: In the 1700s, families loaded their whole lives onto ox wagons and rolled into the interior. But the land wasn't empty.
clip_script: Big families, no land left near the Cape, and a Company with too many rules. So the trekboers loaded their wagons and drove their sheep and cattle inland, onto huge loan farms in the Karoo and beyond. They made their own soap and shoes, read the family Bible, and went to town once a year. Their herders, guides and drivers were mostly Khoikhoi, who had lost their own land and cattle. As hunting grounds vanished, the San fought back, and commandos answered with terrible violence. In the east, the trekboers met the Xhosa. A new frontier had begun.
visual_style: An ox wagon crosses a wide Karoo landscape at sunrise, followed by sheep and herders; a San rock painting appears on a cliff in the foreground; the map shows arrows moving north and east.
pacing: Slow and wide, then sharper at the conflict.
